lly%2C%20a%20convenient%20minimal%20set)%20to%20describe%20the%20configuration%20of%20the%20system%20taking%20into%20account%20its%20constraints.%20For%20a%20system%20with%20multiple%20bodies%20and%20several%20constraints%2C%20e.g.%2C%20the%20human%20body%2C%20it%20is%20easier%20to%20describe%20the%20dynamics%20of%20such%20system%20using%20the%20Langrangian%20formalism.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Zajac%20and%20Gordon%20(1989)%20and%20Zajac%20(1993)%20offer%20excellent%20discussions%20about%20applying%20multibody%20system%20concepts%20to%20understanding%20human%20body%20movement.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Next%2C%20we%20will%20study%20two%20simple%20problems%20of%20multibody%20systems%20in%20the%20context%20of%20biomechanics%20which%20we%20can%20handle%20well%20using%20the%20Newton-Euler%20approach.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20First%20a%20planar%20one-link%20system%20(which%20is%20not%20a%20multibody)%2C%20which%20can%20represent%20the%20movement%20of%20one%20limb%20of%20the%20body%20or%20the%20entire%20body%20as%20a%20single%20inverted%20pendulum.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20Second%2C%20a%20planar%20two-link%20system%2C%20which%20can%20represent%20the%20movement%20of%20two%20segments%20of%20the%20body%2C%20e.g.%2C%20upper%20arm%20and%20forearm.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Newton-Euler%20equations%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20a%20two-dimensional%20movement%20in%20the%20%24XY%24%20plane%2C%20the%20Newton-Euler%20equations%20are%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Baligned%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cleft%5C%7B%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Csum%20F_X%20%26%3D%26%20m%20%5Cddot%7Bx%7D_%7Bcm%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Csum%20F_Y%20%26%3D%26%20m%20%5Cddot%7By%7D_%7Bcm%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Csum%20M_Z%20%26%3D%26%20I_%7Bcm%7D%20%5Cddot%7B%5Calpha%7D_Z%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%20%5Cright.%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Baligned%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%20the%20movement%20is%20described%20around%20the%20body%20center%20of%20mass%20(%24cm%24).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%24(F_X%2C%5C%2CF_Y)%24%20and%20%24M_Z%24%20are%2C%20respectively%2C%20the%20forces%20and%20moment%20of%20forces%20(torques)%20acting%20on%20the%20body.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%24(%5Cddot%7Bx%7D_%7Bcm%7D%2C%5C%2C%5Cddot%7By%7D_%7Bcm%7D)%24%20and%20%24%5Cddot%7B%5Calpha%7D_Z%24%20are%2C%20respectively%2C%20the%20linear%20and%20angular%20accelerations.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%24I_%7Bcm%7D%24%20is%20the%20body%20moment%20of%20inertia%20around%20the%20body%20center%20of%20mass%20at%20the%20%24Z%24%20axis.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20use%20Sympy%20to%20derive%20some%20of%20the%20characteristics%20of%20the%20systems.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20sympy%20as%20sym%0A%20%20%20%20from%20sympy%20import%20Symbol%2C%20symbols%2C%20cos%2C%20sin%2C%20Matrix%2C%20simplify%0A%20%20%20%20from%20sympy.vector%20import%20CoordSys3D%0A%20%20%20%20from%20sympy.physics.mechanics%20import%20dynamicsymbols%2C%20mlatex%2C%20init_vprinting%0A%20%20%20%20init_vprinting()%0A%20%20%20%20from%20IPython.display%20import%20display%2C%20Math%0A%0A%20%20%20%20eq%20%3D%20lambda%20lhs%2C%20rhs%3A%20display(Math(lhs%20%2B%20'%3D'%20%2B%20mlatex(rhs)))%0A%20%20%20%20eq%20%3D%20lambda%20lhs%2C%20rhs%3A%20display(Math(r'%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D'%20%2B%20lhs%20%2B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20'%26%3D%26'%20%2B%20mlatex(rhs)%20%2B%20r'%5Cend%7Barray%7D'))%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20CoordSys3D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20Math%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20Matrix%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20Symbol%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20cos%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20display%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20dynamicsymbols%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20eq%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mlatex%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20simplify%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20sin%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20symbols%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20One-link%20system%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20study%20the%20dynamics%20of%20a%20planar%20inverted%20pendulum%20as%20a%20model%20for%20the%20movement%20of%20a%20human%20body%20segment%20with%20an%20external%20force%20acting%20on%20the%20segment%20(see%20Figure%201).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Finvpend1.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20alt%3D%22Inverted%20pendulum%22%2F%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure%201.%20Planar%20inverted%20pendulum%20(one%20link%20attached%20to%20a%20fixed%20body%20by%20a%20hinge%20joint%20in%20a%20plane)%20with%20a%20joint%20actuators%20and%20corresponding%20free%20body%20diagram%20as%20a%20model%20of%20a%20human%20body%20segment.%20See%20text%20for%20notation%20convention.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20following%20notation%20convention%20will%20be%20used%20for%20this%20problem%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24L%24%20is%20the%20length%20of%20the%20segment.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24d%24%20is%20the%20distance%20from%20the%20joint%20of%20the%20segment%20to%20its%20center%20of%20mass%20position.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24m%24%20is%20the%20mass%20of%20the%20segment.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24g%24%20is%20the%20gravitational%20acceleration%20(%2B).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24%5Calpha%24%20is%20the%20angular%20position%20of%20the%20joint%20w.r.t.%20horizontal%2C%20%24%5Cddot%7B%5Calpha_i%7D%24%20is%20the%20corresponding%20angular%20acceleration.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24I%24%20is%20the%20moment%20of%20inertia%20of%20the%20segment%20around%20its%20center%20of%20mass%20position.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24F_%7Br%7D%24%20is%20the%20joint%20reaction%20force.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24F_%7Be%7D%24%20is%20the%20external%20force%20acting%20on%20the%20segment.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24T%24%20is%20the%20joint%20moment%20of%20force%20(torque).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20the%20case%20of%20a%20human%20body%20segment%2C%20muscles%20responsible%20for%20the%20movement%20of%20the%20segment%20are%20represented%20as%20a%20single%20pair%20of%20antagonistic%20joint%20actuators%20(e.g.%2C%20flexors%20and%20extensors).%20We%20will%20consider%20that%20all%20joint%20torques%20are%20generated%20only%20by%20these%20muscles%20(we%20will%20disregard%20the%20torques%20generated%20by%20ligaments%20and%20other%20tissues)%20and%20the%20total%20or%20net%20joint%20torque%20will%20be%20the%20sum%20of%20the%20torques%20generated%20by%20the%20two%20muscles%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20T%20%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%20T_%7Bnet%7D%20%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%20T_%7Bextension%7D%20-%20T_%7Bflexion%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%20we%20considered%20the%20extensor%20torque%20as%20positive%20(counter-clockwise).%20In%20what%20follows%2C%20we%20will%20determine%20only%20the%20net%20torque%20and%20we%20will%20be%20unable%20to%20decompose%20the%20net%20torque%20in%20its%20components.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%202%20%E2%80%94%20Distinguish%20joint%20and%20segment%20angles.**%20The%20first%20segment%20is%20at%20%2430%5E%5Ccirc%24%20to%20horizontal%20and%20the%20second%20joint%20angle%20relative%20to%20it%20is%20%2460%5E%5Ccirc%24.%20What%20is%20the%20second%20segment%20angle%3F%20If%20their%20rates%20are%202%20and%20%E2%88%921%20rad%2Fs%2C%20what%20is%20its%20angular%20velocity%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Solution%20to%20Exercise%202'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Ctheta_2%3D%5Calpha_1%2B%5Calpha_2%3D90%5E%5Ccirc%24%20and%20%24%5Cdot%5Ctheta_2%3D2-1%3D1%24%20rad%2Fs.%20Adding%20angles%20and%20rates%20is%20specific%20to%20this%20planar%20convention%3B%20mixing%20joint%20and%20segment%20variables%20changes%20the%20equations.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Kinetics%0A%0A%20%20%20%20From%20the%20free%20body%20diagram%2C%20the%20Newton-Euler%20equations%20for%20the%20planar%20inverted%20pendulum%20are%20(writing%20the%20equation%20for%20the%20torques%20around%20the%20center%20of%20mass)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20F_%7Br%2Cx%7D%20%2B%20F_%7Be%2Cx%7D%20%26%20%3D%20%26%20m%5Cddot%7Bx%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20F_%7Br%2Cy%7D%20-%20mg%20%2B%20F_%7Be%2Cy%7D%20%26%20%3D%20%26%20m%5Cddot%7By%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20T%20%2B%20dF_%7Br%2Cx%7D%5Csin%5Calpha%20-%20dF_%7Br%2Cy%7D%5Ccos%5Calpha%20-%20(L-d)F_%7Be%2Cx%7D%5Csin%5Calpha%20%2B%20(L-d)F_%7Be%2Cy%7D%5Ccos%5Calpha%20%26%20%3D%20%26%20I%5Cddot%7B%5Calpha%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20However%2C%20manually%20placing%20the%20terms%20in%20the%20Newton-Euler%20equations%20as%20we%20did%20above%20where%20we%20calculated%20the%20signs%20of%20the%20cross%20products%20is%20error%20prone.%20We%20can%20avoid%20this%20manual%20placing%20by%20treating%20the%20quantities%20as%20vectors%20and%20express%20them%20in%20matricial%20form%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7BF%7D%7D_r%20%2B%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7BF%7D%7D_g%20%2B%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7BF%7D%7D_e%20%26%3D%26%20m%5Cddot%7B%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7BT%7D%7D%20%2B%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D_%7Bcm%2Cj%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7BF%7D%7D_r%20%2B%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D_%7Bcm%2Ce%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7BF%7D%7D_e%20%26%3D%26%20I%5Cddot%7B%5Cvec%7B%5Cmathbf%7B%5Calpha%7D%7D%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20F_%7Brx%7D%20%5C%5C%20F_%7Bry%7D%20%5C%5C%200%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%20%2B%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%200%20%5C%5C%20-g%20%5C%5C%200%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%20%2B%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20F_%7Bex%7D%20%5C%5C%20F_%7Bey%7D%20%5C%5C%200%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%26%3D%26%20m%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%5Cddot%7Bx%7D%20%5C%5C%20%5Cddot%7By%7D%20%5C%5C%200%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%2C%20%5Cquad%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%5Chat%7Bi%7D%20%5C%5C%20%5Chat%7Bj%7D%20%5C%5C%20%5Chat%7Bk%7D%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%5C%5C%20T_z%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%20%2B%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20-d%5Ccos%5Calpha%20%5C%5C%20-d%5Csin%5Calpha%20%5C%5C%200%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20F_%7Brx%7D%20%5C%5C%20F_%7Bry%7D%20%5C%5C%200%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%2B%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20(L-d)%5Ccos%5Calpha%20%5C%5C%20(L-d)%5Csin%5Calpha%20%5C%5C%200%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20F_%7Bex%7D%20%5C%5C%20F_%7Bey%7D%20%5C%5C%200%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%26%3D%26%20I_z%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%5C%5C%20%5Cddot%7B%5Calpha%7D%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%2C%20%5Cquad%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%5Chat%7Bi%7D%20%5C%5C%20%5Chat%7Bj%7D%20%5C%5C%20%5Chat%7Bk%7D%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Note%20that%20%24%5Ctimes%24%20represents%20the%20cross%20product%2C%20not%20matrix%20multiplication.%20Then%2C%20both%20in%20symbolic%20or%20numeric%20manipulation%20we%20would%20use%20the%20cross%20product%20function%20to%20perform%20part%20of%20the%20calculations.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20There%20are%20different%20computational%20tools%20that%20can%20be%20used%20for%20the%20formulation%20of%20the%20equations%20of%20motion.%20For%20instance%2C%20Sympy%20has%20a%20module%2C%20%5BClassical%20Mechanics%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fdocs.sympy.org%2Fdev%2Fmodules%2Fphysics%2Fmechanics%2F)%2C%20and%20see%20%5Bthis%20list%5D(http%3A%2F%2Freal.uwaterloo.ca%2F~mbody%2F%23Software)%20for%20other%20software.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20continue%20with%20the%20explicit%20manual%20formulation%20of%20the%20equations%20for%20now.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20can%20rewrite%20the%20equation%20for%20the%20moments%20of%20force%20in%20a%20form%20that%20doesn't%20explicitly%20involve%20the%20joint%20reaction%20force%20expressing%20the%20moments%20of%20force%20around%20the%20joint%20center%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20T%20-%20mgd%5Ccos%5Calpha%20-%20LF_%7Be%2Cx%7D%5Csin%5Calpha%20%2B%20LF_%7Be%2Cy%7D%5Ccos%5Calpha%20%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%20I_o%5Cddot%7B%5Calpha%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%20%24I_o%24%20is%20the%20moment%20of%20inertia%20around%20the%20joint%2C%20%24I_o%3DI_%7Bcm%7D%2Bmd%5E2%24%2C%20using%20the%20parallel%20axis%20theorem.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20torque%20due%20to%20the%20joint%20reaction%20force%20does%20not%20appear%20on%20this%20equation%3B%20this%20torque%20is%20null%20because%20by%20the%20definition%20the%20reaction%20force%20acts%20on%20the%20joint.%20If%20we%20want%20to%20determine%20the%20joint%20torque%20and%20we%20know%20the%20kinematics%2C%20we%20perform%20inverse%20dynamics%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20T%20%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%20I_o%5Cddot%7B%5Calpha%7D%20%2B%20mgd%20%5Ccos%20%5Calpha%20%2B%20LF_%7Be%2Cx%7D%5Csin%5Calpha%20-%20LF_%7Be%2Cy%7D%5Ccos%5Calpha%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20If%20we%20want%20to%20determine%20the%20kinematics%20and%20we%20know%20the%20joint%20torque%2C%20we%20perform%20direct%20dynamics%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cddot%7B%5Calpha%7D%20%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%20I_o%5E%7B-1%7D%5BT%20-%20mgd%20%5Ccos%20%5Calpha%20-%20LF_%7Be%2Cx%7D%5Csin%5Calpha%20%2B%20LF_%7Be%2Cy%7D%5Ccos%5Calpha%20%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20expression%20above%20is%20a%20second-order%20differential%20equation%20which%20typically%20is%20solved%20numerically.%20So%2C%20unless%20we%20are%20explicitly%20interested%20in%20estimating%20the%20joint%20reaction%20forces%2C%20we%20don't%20need%20to%20use%20them%20for%20calculating%20the%20joint%20torque%20or%20simulate%20movement.%20Anyway%2C%20let's%20look%20at%20the%20kinematics%20of%20this%20problem%20to%20introduce%20some%20important%20concepts%20which%20will%20be%20needed%20later.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Kinematics%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20single%20planar%20inverted%20pendulum%20has%20one%20degree%20of%20freedom%2C%20the%20rotation%20movement%20of%20the%20segment%20around%20the%20pin%20joint.%20In%20this%20case%2C%20if%20the%20angular%20position%20%24%5Calpha(t)%24%20is%20known%2C%20the%20coordinates%20%24x(t)%24%20and%20%24y(t)%24%20of%20the%20center%20of%20mass%20and%20their%20derivatives%20can%20be%20readily%20determined%20(a%20process%20referred%20as%20%5Bforward%20kinematics)%5D(kinematic_chain.py%23forward-and-inverse-kinematics)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(Symbol%2C%20dynamicsymbols%2C%20symbols)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20t%20%3D%20Symbol('t')%0A%20%20%20%20d%2C%20L%20%3D%20symbols('d%20L'%2C%20positive%3DTrue)%0A%20%20%20%20a%20%3D%20dynamicsymbols('alpha')%0A%20%20%20%20return%20L%2C%20a%2C%20d%2C%20t%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(a%2C%20cos%2C%20d%2C%20eq%2C%20sin%2C%20t)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20x%2C%20y%20%3D%20d*cos(a)%2C%20d*sin(a)%0A%20%20%20%20xd%2C C%20e.g.%2C%20at%20%24%5Calpha_1%3D-90%5Eo%24%20and%20%24%5Calpha_2%3D0%24%20the%20pendulum%20is%20hanging%20vertical.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%23%20WARNING%3A%20%24F_r%24%20is%20not%20the%20actual%20joint%20reaction%20force!%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20these%20two%20examples%2C%20in%20the%20Newton-Euler%20equations%20based%20on%20the%20free%20body%20diagrams%20we%20represented%20the%20consequences%20of%20all%20possible%20muscle%20forces%20on%20a%20joint%20as%20a%20net%20muscle%20torque%20and%20all%20forces%20acting%20on%20a%20joint%20as%20a%20resultant%20joint%20reaction%20force.%20That%20is%2C%20all%20forces%20between%20segments%20were%20represented%20as%20a%20resultant%20force%20that%20doesn't%20generate%20torque%20and%20a%20force%20couple%20(or%20free%20moment)%20that%20only%20generates%20torque.%20This%20is%20an%20important%20principle%20in%20mechanics%20of%20rigid%20bodies%2C%20see%20for%20example%20%5Bthis%20text%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ffree_body_diagram.py).%20However%2C%20this%20principle%20creates%20the%20unrealistic%20notion%20that%20the%20sum%20of%20forces%20is%20applied%20directly%20on%20the%20joint%20(which%20has%20no%20further%20implication%20for%20a%20rigid%20body)%2C%20but%20it%20is%20inaccurate%20for%20the%20understanding%20of%20the%20local%20effects%20on%20the%20joint.%20So%2C%20if%20we%20are%20trying%20to%20understand%20the%20stress%20on%20the%20joint%20or%20mechanisms%20of%20joint%20injury%2C%20the%20forces%20acting%20on%20the%20joint%20and%20on%20the%20rest%20of%20the%20segment%20must%20be%20considered%20individually.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%23%20Determination%20of%20muscle%20force%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20torque%20%24T%24%20exerted%20by%20a%20muscle%20is%20given%20by%20the%20product%20between%20the%20muscle-tendon%20moment%20arm%20%24r%24%20and%20its%20force%20%24F%24.%20For%20the%20human%20body%2C%20there%20is%20more%20than%20one%20muscle%20crossing%20a%20joint%20and%20several%20joints.%20In%20such%20case%2C%20the%20torques%20due%20to%20the%20muscles%20are%20expressed%20in%20the%20following%20matrix%20form%20considering%20%24n%24%20joints%20and%20%24m%24%20muscles%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Baligned%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20T_1%20%5C%5C%20%5Cvdots%20%5C%5C%20T_n%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%26%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%26%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20r_%7B11%7D%20%26%20%5Ccdots%20%26%20r_%7B1m%7D%20%5C%5C%20%5Cvdots%20%26%20%5Cddots%20%26%20%5Cvdots%20%5C%5C%20r_%7Bn1%7D%20%26%20%5Ccdots%20%26%20r_%7Bnm%7D%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20F_1%20%5C%5C%20%5Cvdots%20%5C%5C%20F_m%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Baligned%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%20%24r_%7Bnm%7D%24%20is%20the%20moment%20arm%20about%20joint%20%24n%24%20of%20the%20muscle%20%24m%24.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20In%20the%20example%20of%20the%20two-link%20system%2C%20we%20sketched%20two%20uniarticular%20muscles%20for%20each%20of%20the%20two%20joints%2C%20consequently%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Baligned%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20T_1%20%5C%5C%20T_2%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%26%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%26%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20r_%7B1%2Cext%7D%20%26%20-r_%7B1%2Cflex%7D%20%26%200%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%26%200%20%26%20r_%7B1%2Cext%7D%20%26%20-r_%7B1%2Cflex%7D%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20F_%7B1%2Cext%7D%20%5C%5C%20F_%7B1%2Cflex%7D%20%5C%5C%20F_%7B2%2Cext%7D%20%5C%5C%20F_%7B2%2Cflex%7D%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Baligned%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Note%20the%20opposite%20signs%20for%20the%20moment%20arms%20of%20the%20extension%20and%20flexion%20muscles%20hence%20they%20generate%20opposite%20torques.%20We%20could%20have%20represented%20the%20opposite%20signs%20in%20the%20muscle%20forces%20instead%20of%20in%20the%20moment%20arms.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20moment%20arm%20of%20a%20muscle%20varies%20with%20the%20motion%20of%20the%20joints%20it%20crosses.%20In%20this%20case%2C%20using%20the%20%5Bvirtual%20work%20principle%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FVirtual_work)%20the%20moment%20arm%20can%20be%20given%20by%20(Sherman%20et%20al.%2C%202013%3B%20Nigg%20and%20Herzog%2C%202006%2C%20page%20634)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20r(q)%20%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%20%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cpartial%20L_%7BMT%7D(q)%7D%7B%5Cpartial%20q%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%20%24L_%7BMT%7D(q)%24%20is%20the%20length%20of%20the%20muscle-tendon%20unit%20expressed%20as%20a%20function%20of%20angle%20%24q%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20the%20simulation%20of%20human%20movement%2C%20muscles%20can%20be%20modeled%20as%20%5BHill-type%20muscles%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_simulation.py)%2C%20the%20torques%20they%20generate%20are%20given%20by%20the%20matrix%20above%2C%20and%20this%20matrix%20is%20entered%20in%20the%20ODE%20for%20a%20multibody%20system%20dynamics%20we%20deduced%20before%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cddot%7Bq%7D%20%5Cquad%3D%5Cquad%20M(q)%5E%7B-1%7D%20%5Cleft%5BR_%7BMT%7D(q)F_%7BMT%7D(a%2CL_%7BMT%7D%2C%5Cdot%7BL%7D_%7BMT%7D)%20-%20C(q%2C%5Cdot%7Bq%7D)%20-%20G(q)%20-%20E(q%2C%5Cdot%7Bq%7D)%20%5Cright%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%20%24R_%7BMT%7D%24%20and%20%24F_%7BMT%7D%24%20are%20matrices%20for%20the%20moment%20arms%20and%20muscle-tendon%20forces%2C%20respectively.%0A%20%20%20%20This%20ODE%20is%20then%20solved%20numerically%20given%20initial%20values%3B%20but%20this%20problem%20is%20far%20from%20trivial%20for%20a%20simulation%20with%20several%20segments%20and%20muscles.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)% ine%20the%20desired%20trajectory%2C%20we%20can%20calculate%20the%20velocity%20and%20acceleration%20of%20the%20segments%20and%20combine%20with%20anthropometric%20measures%20to%20calculate%20the%20joint%20torques%20necessary%20to%20move%20the%20segments.%20This%20means%20we%20will%20perform%20inverse%20dynamics.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20simulate%20a%20slow%20(4%20s)%20and%20a%20fast%20(0.5%20s)%20movement%20of%20the%20upper%20limb%20starting%20at%20the%20anatomical%20neutral%20position%20(upper%20limb%20at%20the%20side%20of%20the%20trunk)%20and%20ending%20with%20the%20upper%20arm%20forward%20at%20horizontal%20and%20elbow%20flexed%20at%2090%20degrees.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20First%2C%20let's%20import%20the%20necessary%20Python%20libraries%20and%20customize%20the%20environment%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20repo_file(path%2C%20*%2C%20base_url%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fmaster%2F%22)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Find%20a%20repository%20file%20beside%20this%20notebook%2C%20or%20fetch%20a%20temporary%20copy.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Local%20files%20take%20precedence.%20Only%20file%20acquisition%20falls%20back%20to%20GitHub%3B%0A%20%20%20%20parsing%20errors%20remain%20visible%20to%20the%20calling%20notebook.%20urllib3%20selects%20its%0A%20%20%20%20browser%20transport%20automatically%20without%20platform-specific%20imports.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20hashlib%0A%20%20%20%20import%20tempfile%0A%20%20%20%20from%20pathlib%20import%20Path%2C%20PurePosixPath%0A%20%20%20%20from%20urllib.parse%20import%20quote%0A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20marimo%20as%20mo%0A%20%20%20%20import%20urllib3%0A%0A%20%20%20%20relative%20%3D%20PurePosixPath(path)%0A%20%20%20%20if%20relative.is_absolute()%20or%20%22..%22%20in%20relative.parts%20or%20%22%5C%5C%22%20in%20str(path)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20raise%20ValueError(%22Use%20a%20repository-relative%20path%20such%20as%20data%2Fwalk.trc%22)%0A%20%20%20%20location%20%3 umerical%20error%20signals%20inconsistent%20models%2C%20signs%20or%20inputs.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Derive%20the%20equations%20of%20motion%20for%20a%20single%20pendulum%20(not%20inverted).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Derive%20the%20equations%20of%20motion%20for%20a%20double%20pendulum%20(not%20inverted).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%203.%20For%20the%20one-link%20system%2C%20simulate%20a%20typical%20trajectory%20to%20calculate%20the%20joint%20torque%20(i.e.%2C%20perform%20inverse%20dynamics).%0A%20%20%20%204.%20For%20the%20one-link%20system%2C%20simulate%20a%20typical%20joint%20torque%20to%20calculate%20the%20trajectory%20(i.e.%2C%20perform%20direct%20dynamics).%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Consider%20the%20double%20pendulum%20moving%20in%20the%20horizontal%20plane%20and%20with%20no%20external%20force.%20Find%20out%20the%20type%20of%20movement%20and%20which%20torque%20terms%20are%20changed%20when%3A%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20a)%20%24%5Cdot%7B%5Calpha%7D_1%3D0%5Eo%24%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20b)%20%24%5Calpha_2%3D0%5Eo%24%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20c)%20%24%5Cdot%7B%5Calpha%7D_2%3D0%5Eo%24%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20d)%20%242%5Calpha_1%2B%5Calpha_2%3D180%5Eo%24%20(hint%3A%20a%20two-link%20system%20with%20this%20configuration%20is%20called%20polar%20manipulator)%0A%20%20%20%206.%20Derive%20the%20equations%20of%20motion%20and%20the%20torque%20terms%20using%20angles%20in%20the%20segmental%20space%20%24(%5Ctheta_1%2C%5C%2C%5Ctheta_2)%24.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%207.%20Run%20the%20numerical%20simulations%20for%20the%20torques%20with%20different%20parameters.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Final%20answers%20to%20original%20Problems'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%201.%20For%20a%20rigid%20link%20with%20center%20distance%20%24r%24%20and%20pivot%20inertia%20%24I_O%24%2C%20angle%20from%20downward%20vertical%3A%20%24I_O%5Cddot%5Ctheta%2Bmgr%5Csin%5Ctheta%3D%5Ctau%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20For%20two%20uniform%20rods%20with%20absolute%20downward-vertical%20angles%2C%20%24M_%7B11%7D%3Dm_1L_1%5E2%2F3%2Bm_2L_1%5E2%24%2C%20%24M_%7B22%7D%3Dm_2L_2%5E2%2F3%24%2C%20%24M_%7B12%7D%3DM_%7B21%7D%3Dm_2L_1L_2%5Ccos(%5Ctheta_1-%5Ctheta_2)%2F2%24.%20The%20velocity-quadratic%20terms%20on%20the%20left%20are%20%24(h%5Cdot%5Ctheta_2%5E2%2C-h%5Cdot%5Ctheta_1%5E2)%5ET%24%2C%20with%20%24h%3Dm_2L_1L_2%5Csin(%5Ctheta_1-%5Ctheta_2)%2F2%24%3B%20gravity%20terms%20are%20%24((m_1%2F2%2Bm_2)gL_1%5Csin%5Ctheta_1%2Cm_2gL_2%5Csin%5Ctheta_2%2F2)%5ET%24.%20Applied%20generalized%20torques%20are%20%24(%5Ctau_1-%5Ctau_2%2C%5Ctau_2)%5ET%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20For%20any%20selected%20one-link%20trajectory%2C%20%24%5Ctau(t)%3DI_O%5Cddot%5Ctheta(t)%2Bmgr%5Csin%5Ctheta(t)%24%20in%20the%20convention%20of%20answer%201.%20Different%20prescribed%20trajectories%20give%20different%20torque%20histories.%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20The%20forward%20result%20solves%20%24%5Cddot%5Ctheta%3D%5B%5Ctau(t)-mgr%5Csin%5Ctheta%5D%2FI_O%24%20with%20two%20stated%20initial%20conditions.%20The%20inverse%20torque%20from%20answer%203%20reproduces%20its%20trajectory%20up%20to%20integration%20error%20when%20the%20initial%20conditions%20match.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20In%20joint%20coordinates%2C%20velocity%20terms%20are%20proportional%20to%20%24-b%5Csin%5Calpha_2(2%5Cdot%5Calpha_1%5Cdot%5Calpha_2%2B%5Cdot%5Calpha_2%5E2)%24%20and%20%24b%5Csin%5Calpha_2%5Cdot%5Calpha_1%5E2%24.%20(a)%20First%20joint%20stationary%3A%20only%20the%20%24%5Cdot%5Calpha_2%5E2%24%20term%20remains.%20(b)%20Straight%20links%3A%20both%20velocity%20terms%20vanish%20instantaneously.%20(c)%20Fixed%20elbow%20angle%3A%20the%20second%20term%20remains%20when%20%24%5Cdot%5Calpha_1%5Cne0%24.%20(d)%20%242%5Calpha_1%2B%5Calpha_2%3D%5Cpi%24%20gives%20a%20straight%20radial%20endpoint%20path%20for%20equal%20link%20lengths%3B%20it%20implies%20%24%5Cdot%5Calpha_2%3D-2%5Cdot%5Calpha_1%24%20and%20makes%20the%20first%20velocity%20term%20zero.%20Unequal%20link%20lengths%20do%20not%20generally%20produce%20that%20radial%20path.%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20With%20%24q%3D(%5Calpha_1%2C%5Calpha_2)%5ET%3DA%5Ctheta%24%2C%20%24A%3D%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D1%260%5C%5C-1%261%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%24%2C%20the%20segment-coordinate%20equation%20is%20%24M_%5Ctheta%3DA%5ETM_qA%24%2C%20%24h_%5Ctheta%3DA%5ETh_q%24%2C%20%24g_%5Ctheta%3DA%5ETg_q%24%20and%20%24%5Ctau_%5Ctheta%3DA%5ET%5Ctau_q%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%207.%20Numerical%20curves%20depend%20on%20the%20chosen%20parameters.%20For%20the%20same%20path%20traversed%20twice%20as%20fast%2C%20inertial%20and%20quadratic-velocity%20torques%20scale%20by%20four%3B%20gravity%20torque%20at%20each%20posture%20is%20unchanged.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Go%20deeper%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Use%20%5BKineticsFundamentalConcepts%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinetics_fundamental_concepts.py)%20to%20connect%20this%20guide%20with%20the%20surrounding%20mechanics%20and%20modeling%20material.%20Return%20to%20the%20assumptions%20behind%20each%20equation%20when%20applying%20it%20to%20a%20new%20experiment.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Video%20lectures%20on%20the%20Internet%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%5BMIT%20OpenCourseWare%5D(https%3A%2F%2Focw.mit.edu%2Fcourses%2F2-003sc-engineering-dynamics-fall-2011%2Fpages%2Flagrange-equations%2F)%20%E2%80%94%20Lagrange%20equations%3A%20follow%20the%20energy-to-equation%20method%20in%20the%20lecture%20a
